title: Longest Stretch With Two Kinds
statement:
A feed shows posts one after another, and topics[i] is the topic id of post i. You want to read one unbroken stretch of consecutive posts that covers at most two different topics.

Return the length of the longest such stretch.

examples.why: [4, 4, 7, 4] uses topics 4 and 7. Adding the 9 would bring in a third topic.
The best stretch is [1, 3, 3, 3, 1]. It starts at the 1 just before the 3s, not right after the 2, so a window that restarts at the new topic misses it.
One topic is fine: "at most two" includes one.

hints: The answer is a contiguous range, and the rule is about what is inside it. That calls for a window with a left and a right end.
Grow the window to the right. When a third topic shows up, which end must move, and how far?
Keep a count per topic inside the window. When the window holds three topics, move the left end forward, decreasing counts and deleting topics that reach zero, until only two remain.

explain.intuition:
If a stretch is valid, every shorter stretch inside it is valid too. So for each right end there is a furthest-left start that still works, and that start only moves forward as the right end moves forward. That is the sliding window shape.

Track how many times each topic appears inside the window. Add the new post on the right; if that makes three topics, drop posts from the left until one topic's count hits zero. The window is then the longest valid one ending here. The second example shows why you shrink one post at a time instead of jumping: the valid stretch can reach back past the post that started the newest run.
steps: While the map has more than two keys: decrement count[topics[left]], delete it if it reached zero, and move left forward.
pitfalls: Restarting the window at the post where the new topic appears. It throws away the run of the other topic just before it, as in example 2.
Counting distinct topics in the whole array, or taking the two most frequent topics. The stretch must be contiguous.
Forgetting to delete a topic from the map when its count drops to zero, so the map size never shrinks.

complexity.space: O(1): the map never holds more than three topics

solutions.title: Every start, grow until a third topic
solutions.idea: From each start, extend to the right while the set of topics has at most two members.

solutions.title: Sliding window with counts
solutions.idea: Grow on the right, count each topic inside the window, and shrink from the left whenever a third topic enters.

solutions.title: Track the last run
solutions.idea: Remember the two topics in the current stretch and how long the latest unbroken run of the newest topic is. When a third topic arrives, the new stretch is that last run plus the new post.
